accepted.sentence: Fixed-jaw versions are manufactured with openings in different sizes to fit fasteners of specific dimensions.
Some pipe-gripping designs have serrated teeth that bite into rounded cylindrical surfaces.
A hanging hole near the handle's end allows the tool to be stored on a peg.
Aluminum-alloy bodies weigh less than steel versions, but may be less suitable for very high loads.
Certain models have a joint between the head and handle that lets the head pivot through a limited arc.
Size markings are often stamped or etched into the metal near the head.
A slim handle profile can fit into tight spaces, while a broader cross-section can resist bending under load.
Some ring-shaped heads have twelve internal points that engage a fastener at several angular positions.
